Temporal and dynamic graphs

Source: vignettes/temporal-graphs.Rmd
temporal-graphs.Rmd
library(graphlearnR)

Graphs change. Messages are sent, payments are made, sensors report every few minutes. graphlearnR supports three views of time, and each comes with a rule that keeps the future out of the past.

view object leakage rule
events in continuous time temporal_graph_data a query at time t uses events with time < t
discrete snapshots snapshot_sequence snapshot k covers [b_k, b_{k+1}); evaluation steps come after training steps
signals on a fixed graph spatiotemporal_signal train, validation, and test windows are consecutive in time

Event graphs

A temporal graph is a stream of timestamped edges, sorted by time on creation. event_id remembers the input order.

tg <- temporal_graph_data(src = c(3, 1, 2, 1), dst = c(1, 2, 3, 3), t = c(5, 1, 3, 7),
                          edge_attr = matrix(c(0.5, 0.1, 0.3, 0.9), ncol = 1))
tg
#> <temporal_graph_data> 3 nodes, 4 events, t in [1, 7]
data.frame(src = tg$src, dst = tg$dst, t = tg$t, event_id = tg$event_id)
#>   src dst t event_id
#> 1   1   2 1        2
#> 2   2   3 3        3
#> 3   3   1 5        1
#> 4   1   3 7        4

Windows and splits

temporal_window() keeps events with start <= t < end. split_temporal() cuts the stream at two times, so every validation event is later than every training event and every test event is later still.

events <- dataset_synthetic_temporal(num_nodes = 30, num_events = 600, seed = 1)
events
#> <temporal_graph_data> 30 nodes, 600 events, t in [0.06052661, 99.63633]
sp <- split_temporal(events, val_time = 60, test_time = 80)
c(train = length(sp$train$t), val = length(sp$val$t), test = length(sp$test$t))
#> train   val  test 
#>   374   109   117
c(max(sp$train$t), min(sp$val$t), max(sp$val$t), min(sp$test$t))
#> [1] 59.88687 60.06185 79.95084 80.04763

Causal neighborhoods

temporal_neighbors() returns the k most recent events of each query node strictly before its query time. With strict = FALSE it also keeps events at exactly the query time; use that only when an event at time t really is known at time t.

nb <- temporal_neighbors(events, nodes = c(1, 2), times = c(50, 50), k = 3,
                         direction = "both")
nb
#>   query node neighbor        t event
#> 1     1    1       16 49.91498   314
#> 2     1    1       12 49.48825   308
#> 3     1    1       16 43.77153   278
#> 4     2    2       26 49.77389   312
#> 5     2    2       20 47.88741   301
#> 6     2    2       20 47.21785   296
all(nb$t < 50)
#> [1] TRUE

Snapshots

temporal_snapshots() bins events into graphs. Each snapshot uses the half open interval [b_k, b_{k+1}); repeated events between the same pair become the edge weight. With cumulative = TRUE snapshot k holds every event before b_{k+1}.

snaps <- temporal_snapshots(events, breaks = 8)
snaps
#> <snapshot_sequence> 8 snapshots of 30 nodes
vapply(snaps$graphs, num_edges, integer(1))
#> [1]  66  80  90 102  90  94 110 102
round(snaps$start, 1)
#> [1]  0.1 12.5 25.0 37.4 49.8 62.3 74.7 87.2

Dynamic link prediction

train_dynamic_link_model() runs a graph GRU over the snapshots. At each training step it predicts the edges of the next snapshot from everything up to the current one, with fresh negatives. Evaluation steps are strictly later than all training steps, and the result carries a baseline that scores a pair by how often it appeared before.

library(torch)
torch_manual_seed(1)
fit <- train_dynamic_link_model(snaps, hidden_dim = 16, epochs = 30, seed = 1)
fit
#> <temporal_fit> dynamic link prediction, 30 epochs
#>   test:      roc_auc = 0.8705, average_precision = 0.8432 
#>   baseline:  roc_auc = 0.8823, average_precision = 0.8624
fit$train_steps
#> [1] 2 3 4 5
fit$eval_steps
#> [1] 6 7 8
fit$step_metrics
#>   step   roc_auc average_precision
#> 1    6 0.8458579         0.8098603
#> 2    7 0.8882645         0.8633798
#> 3    8 0.8773549         0.8562412
rbind(model = fit$test_metrics, history_baseline = fit$baseline_metrics)
#>                    roc_auc average_precision
#> model            0.8704924         0.8431605
#> history_baseline 0.8823424         0.8624293

Report the model next to the baseline. On many real dynamic graphs, simply predicting that past edges repeat is hard to beat, and a model that does not beat it has not learned anything new.

Spatiotemporal signals

A spatiotemporal signal is a fixed graph (a road network, a sensor grid) with a feature array of shape time by nodes by features.

sig <- dataset_synthetic_signal(num_nodes = 15, num_steps = 80, seed = 2)
sig
#> <spatiotemporal_signal> 80 steps, 15 nodes, 1 features
dim(sig$features)
#> [1] 80 15  1

train_spatiotemporal_model() forecasts horizon steps ahead from lags past steps with a graph GRU. Windows are assigned to training, validation, and test sets in time order, and the naive forecast (the last observed value) is reported next to the model.

torch_manual_seed(2)
fst <- train_spatiotemporal_model(sig, lags = 4, horizon = 1, hidden_dim = 16,
                                  epochs = 40, seed = 2)
fst
#> <temporal_fit> spatiotemporal forecasting, 40 epochs
#>   test:      mse = 0.009564, mae = 0.07996 
#>   baseline:  mse = 0.01375, mae = 0.09504
c(last_train = max(fst$windows$train), first_val = min(fst$windows$val),
  first_test = min(fst$windows$test))
#> last_train  first_val first_test 
#>         56         57         68
rbind(model = fst$test_metrics, naive = fst$baseline_metrics)
#>              mse        mae
#> model 0.00956420 0.07995598
#> naive 0.01375186 0.09503502

To bring your own data, build the graph with any of the constructors and pass the array to spatiotemporal_signal(), which checks that the node dimension matches.

Memory based models: TGN

Snapshot models see the graph at a fixed resolution. A temporal graph network (Rossi et al. 2020) works on the event stream directly. Every node has a memory vector, a GRU updates it each time the node takes part in an event, and the embedding used for prediction combines the memory with the time since the last update and, optionally, the node’s most recent partners.

train_tgn() processes the training events in chronological batches. Each batch is scored with the memory left by earlier batches only, and its own events update memory at the start of the next batch, so no event ever informs its own prediction. Validation and test continue the same memory in time order without gradient updates.

stream <- dataset_synthetic_temporal(num_events = 1500, seed = 1)
sp_t <- split_temporal(stream)
torch_manual_seed(1)
tgn <- tgn_model(stream$num_nodes, memory_dim = 32, time_dim = 8, embedding_dim = 32)
fit_tgn <- train_tgn(tgn, sp_t, epochs = 10, batch_size = 50, lr = 0.01, seed = 1)
fit_tgn$history
#>    epoch train_loss   val_auc
#> 1      1  0.6624339 0.6485333
#> 2      2  0.5714008 0.7299160
#> 3      3  0.4855788 0.8057086
#> 4      4  0.4264535 0.8403753
#> 5      5  0.3848646 0.8578963
#> 6      6  0.3400036 0.8775309
#> 7      7  0.3274034 0.8930765
#> 8      8  0.3020271 0.8911210
#> 9      9  0.2973747 0.8774914
#> 10    10  0.2969318 0.8906667
fit_tgn$test_metrics
#>           roc_auc average_precision 
#>         0.8712898         0.8767697

Each event is scored against one random destination. The synthetic stream repeats earlier pairs often, so memory and the learned node embeddings (node_embedding = TRUE, the default) carry most of the signal.

The embedding can also look at each node’s most recent partners. With embedding = "graph_attention", the variant the TGN paper found best, multi head attention runs over the num_neighbors latest partners; keys and values combine the partner’s memory, the time since that interaction and the event features, and the query comes from the node’s own memory. Only partners from earlier batches are visible, for the same reason as above.

torch_manual_seed(1)
tgn_att <- tgn_model(stream$num_nodes, memory_dim = 32, time_dim = 8, embedding_dim = 32,
                     embedding = "graph_attention", num_neighbors = 5, heads = 2)
fit_att <- train_tgn(tgn_att, sp_t, epochs = 10, batch_size = 50, lr = 0.01, seed = 1)
fit_att$test_metrics
#>           roc_auc average_precision 
#>         0.8633801         0.8615132

The implementation has one embedding layer (one hop) and keeps the most recent message per node; the paper’s other message aggregators are not included.

The recurrent cell

graph_gru_cell() replaces the matrix products of a GRU with graph convolutions, as in DCRNN and GConvGRU, so the hidden state of each node mixes with its neighbors at every step. temporal_gnn_model() wraps it with an output layer. Its output at step s depends only on inputs up to step s; the test suite checks this by changing later inputs and comparing.

g <- sig$graph
tt <- graph_tensors(g)
torch_manual_seed(3)
m <- temporal_gnn_model(input_dim = 1, hidden_dim = 8, output_dim = 1)
xs <- lapply(1:5, function(s) torch_tensor(matrix(sig$features[s, , 1], ncol = 1)))
out <- m(xs, tt$edge_index)
length(out$outputs)
#> [1] 5
dim(out$outputs[[5]])
#> [1] 15  1
